sources.title: ESO E-ELT Design Reference Mission: AO performance and PSFs (technical data)
sources.locator: 'Atmosphere' and 'Parameters of layers' tables; system/simulation parameter table; PSF database description
supports: integrated Fried parameter r0 = 0.13 m at 500 nm (seeing 0.8 arcsec), von Karman spectrum, outer scale 25 m, inner scale = pixel size
ten turbulent layers 0-18.5 km with fractional Cn2 (printed sum 1.001) and wind speeds 8.0-33.7 m/s; wind directions not published
84x84 Shack-Hartmann scale and an 85x85 ground-conjugate DM with linear-spline influence family
500 Hz loop rate, 2000 iterations (4 s), a three-iteration command delay
idealized (noiseless) sensing in the simulation parameter set
limitations: the PSF database covers GLAO, LTAO and NOAO only; there is no SCAO PSF to compare against
the system scales come from multi-conjugate/LGS studies and are borrowed into a one-NGS SCAO topology
the CCD sampling row reads '6' without a dimensional interpretation; it is not used as a 6x6 detector claim
the linear-spline basis is named, not defined; the separable bilinear tent is an assumption (A06)

sources.title: ESO E-ELT Design Reference Mission: telescope technical data
supports: central-obstruction diameter ratio 0.28 (annular collecting area pi/4 D^2 (1 - 0.28^2))
limitations: segmentation, spiders and gaps are omitted in this reference case
the historical 42 m design differs from the current 39 m ELT

sources.title: S. Gladysz and R. Rebolo, The E-ELT Design Reference Mission: Direct imaging of terrestrial and giant exoplanets (DRM report S3, v2)
supports: a separate SCAO case: spatially filtered SH 84x84, 2 ms integration, 6 ms readout-plus-reconstruction lag, 3 e- read noise, 0.6-0.9 um sensing, 30 nm NCPA
limitations: PAOLA-based analytic method with 0.7 arcsec seeing, its own pupil and perfect spatial filtering
its lag definition differs from the R1 delayed-command convention; values are not merged into the normative case

sources.title: C. Bechet and M. Tallon, Reducing the Fractal Iterative Method (FRiM) to the cost of half an iteration, ESO RTC workshop 2012
supports: an independent FRiM/OCTOPUS SCAO experiment: 42 m, obstruction 0.28, 500 Hz, nine layers, r0 = 0.129 m, tau0 = 2.8 ms, ground DM 85x85, one NGS, SH 84x84, 1e5 photons/frame/subaperture
limitations: slides, not a complete reproducible input deck or a raw SCAO PSF dataset
its nine-layer profile is not the packaged ten-layer R1 profile; substituting one for the other is not a reproduction

reference_cases.why_not_runnable: analytic PAOLA study with a different atmosphere, pupil, filtering, noise and lag convention; no end-to-end input deck
the nine-layer profile, noise model and reconstruction details are not published in reproducible form

contradictions.description: R1 states a delayed command of three iteration intervals; R3 states a 2 ms integration and a 6 ms readout-plus-reconstruction lag.
contradictions.resolution: the normative benchmark uses R1 (latency_frames = 2, total measured-to-applied delay three frame intervals, A10); R3 stays a separate reference case.

contradictions.description: R1 gives 10 layers with r0 = 0.13 m; R4 gives 9 layers with r0 = 0.129 m.
contradictions.resolution: the benchmark uses the packaged R1 ten-layer profile; R4 is not reproduced.

contradictions.description: R1 assumes idealized sensing; R3 uses 3 e- read noise; R4 uses 1e5 photons per frame per subaperture.
contradictions.resolution: deterministic noiseless sensing with a declared numerical electron scale (A09); no noise model is borrowed from R3 or R4.

contradictions.description: R1 seeing 0.8 arcsec versus R3 0.7 arcsec.
contradictions.resolution: r0 = 0.13 m at 500 nm from R1 is primary.
